## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [21. Januar 1942], SZ-AAL/B1.191
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.191
- Datum: 21.1.1942
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 5 Scans

pages.transcription:
21. I 1942 Petropolis (Brasil) 34 rua Gonçalves Dias
Dear Hannah & Manfred, we had today news about Eva from Mrs. Weaffer
and Petropolis[?] ; she had a great Christmas time at fabulous and
is invited for Easter again; she was at Mrs. Weaffer and with my sister in law
in the Metropolitan Opera at the 'Magic Flute' and in Radio City, it seems
she has enjoyed it. My sister in law complains somewhat about a
certain untidiness ~~at~~ in her costume and that Mrs. Weaffer should be more
strict in this sense; I believe that, when Eva will come into the dangerous
years ~~of~~ of love she will herself do her best to look attractive and neat.
My sister in law is, as I told you before not exactly a cheerful person,
she likes to find out, that others do not care enough for her children -
I think she finds also that we have been cruel not to take Eva to
Brazil - but anyhow she is the only one which has not much to do and
she likes to go with Eva, so one has to pardon her some exaggeration and
hysteries. It is not pleasant for me that my brother and his wife
are so special and full of fears and other complexes; how easy would
it have been if they would have been normal and easy, but being
somewhat a fool myself I have no right to complain. The most im-
portant thing is that apart from a certain carelessness about her -
sonal appearance Eva is well educated there, feels at home as
much as it is possible in your absence and has the absolutely right
surrounding; we do and I feel absolutely sure about Mrs. Weaffer.
There was in the American newspapers a note, that it is now
allowed to parents in England to send to her children a pocket-money
of about 12 dollars a month. I think you should do that, I believe
that Eva will be proud to get a little private money from her parents
directly as we cannot send her anything from here (it would be ne-
cessary to ask for permissions etc) and I know how proud a child is to
have something of her own. From us is not much to tell. The weather
has finally cleared up and we make long walks, Lotte feels much
better, her attacks have nearly ceased, only at night to wakes up
(and wakes me up) once or twice for a little coughing and her weight
is far from satisfying me, but I have to take her as I took her and
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf dünnem Papier. Tinte violett. Die Rückseite des Blattes (Scan 2) zeigt den durchscheinenden Text der Vorderseite.
Rückseite des Dokuments, leer (abgesehen vom durchscheinenden Text der Vorderseite).

pages.transcription:
The law does not allow to send her back only because she has two or three
kilogramms less weight than before. From the conference at Rio we see
not more than you read in the papers, our little dog is sweet but be-
haves badly, strolling away in the neighborhood, especially in cafes
or houses with children and for the third time negros brought him back.
Perhaps he finds life a little too tedious with a single couple and I
find it tedious myself sometimes; we have books but one feels some-
what isolated - on the other hand, there is no place in this war world
where you feel less interference from the war. Our solitude has the
bad effect that my Portuguese does make no progress at all - there
is also some inherent repression in me; when I studied French
English and Italian at fifteen, I knew that I made an effort for
forty or fifty years and that was worth while. And for how many
or better for how few years shall I study Portuguese? Lotte learns
much better as the house-hold obliges her to conversation. I be-
lieve we told you that the workman who lives in a hut connected
with our bungalow got a baby, a tiny creature; so Lotte does have
some 'treat' by it and the boy, but she is not so interested in it
as I supposed. — We follow every line in the papers about
England and the war. We are so glad that there was no more bom-
bing since months, but all seems to indicate that the war will be
still a very long one as the real preparations in the U.S. which
are enormous have not yet the full activity in the battle but nobody
can realize how enormous they are. I continue to work, in the
U.S.A we find not yet the right translator for the autobiography
but next month will appear the little booklet about Amerigo Ves-
pucci and I am working here on another book. We will soon
know if we can have this bungalow longer than April - the
house is somewhat damp and shoes and all leather things, even
books, gets (mouldy) [eingefügt] mistiness after one day of rain, but we hate changing
landing, new address and would like to remain. Now I have only
written about us and nothing about you but you know that all
our wishes we are with you. Love to all - Stefan

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, die Handschrift von Stefan Zweig ist klar. Die Farbskalen verdecken teilweise den Text, dieser ist jedoch durch die anderen Scans vollständig rekonstruierbar.
